Core plugin structure & rule registry: - src/index.ts exports the plugin surface: - Top-level JSDoc: /** * ESLint Traceability Plugin * @story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md * @req REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE - Provide foundational plugin export and registration * @req REQ-ERROR-HANDLING - Gracefully handles plugin loading errors and missing dependencies */ - Dynamic rule registry: const RULE_NAMES = [ "require-story-annotation", "require-req-annotation", "require-branch-annotation", "valid-annotation-format", "valid-story-reference", "valid-req-reference", "prefer-implements-annotation", ] as const; const rules: Record = {} as any; RULE_NAMES.forEach((name) => { try { const mod = require(`./rules/${name}`); rules[name] = mod.default ?? mod; } catch (error: any) { console.error(`...[eslint-plugin-traceability] Failed to load rule "${name}": ${error.message}`); rules[name] = { meta: {...}, create(context) { ... } } as Rule.RuleModule; } }); - Flat-config aware configs & severities: const TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES: Readonly<Record> = { ... }; function createTraceabilityFlatConfig() { return { plugins: { traceability: {} }, rules: { ...TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES } }; } const configs = { recommended: [createTraceabilityFlatConfig()], strict: [createTraceabilityFlatConfig()], }; - ESLint plugin exports: export { rules, configs, maintenance }; export default { rules, configs, maintenance }; → Implements REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE, REQ-RULE-REGISTRY, REQ-CONFIG-SYSTEM, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING.
Rule implementations & TypeScript usage: - Rules implemented in TypeScript under src/rules/*.ts (e.g. src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts, require-req-annotation.ts, require-branch-annotation.ts, valid-annotation-format.ts, valid-story-reference.ts, valid-req-reference.ts, prefer-implements-annotation.ts). - tsconfig.json: - "module": "CommonJS", "outDir": "lib", "declaration": true, "strict": true - "include": ["src", "tests"] → Satisfies REQ-TYPESCRIPT and REQ-NPM-PACKAGE (buildable TS -> lib for npm).
ESLint v9 flat config integration: - Project flat config: eslint.config.js (CommonJS): - Uses @eslint/js and @typescript-eslint/parser. - Dynamically resolves the plugin from source or built output: try { plugin = require("./src/index.js"); } catch { plugin = require("./lib/src/index.js"); ... } - Registers plugin into flat config: { files: ["**/*.ts", "**/*.tsx"], languageOptions: { parser: typescriptParser, parserOptions: { project: "./tsconfig.json", ... } }, plugins: { ...(plugin.rules ? { traceability: plugin } : {}) }, rules: { ... } } - Similar registration for JS files and a special case for tests/integration/cli-integration.test.ts. → Demonstrates ESLint v9 flat-config integration using this plugin (REQ-ESLINT-COMPAT).
Tests specifically for this story: - tests/plugin-setup.test.ts /** * Tests for: docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md * @story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md * @req REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE - plugin exports rules and configs */ import plugin, { rules, configs } from "../src/index"; it("[REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE] plugin exports rules and configs", () => { expect(rules).toBeDefined(); expect(configs).toBeDefined(); expect(typeof rules).toBe("object"); expect(typeof configs).toBe("object"); expect(plugin.rules).toBe(rules); expect(plugin.configs).toBe(configs); }); → Verifies core plugin exports and registration.
- tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts /** * Tests for: docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md * @story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md * @story docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md * @req REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE - Validate plugin default export and configs in src/index.ts * @req REQ-ERROR-SEVERITY - Validate error severity configuration in plugin configs */ - Confirms plugin.default includes rules and configs. - Asserts rules object keys match all expected rule names. - Asserts configs.recommended has correct rule configuration (traceability/* mapped to severities). - Asserts configs.strict mirrors recommended and preserves severity mapping. → Covers REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE, REQ-RULE-REGISTRY, REQ-CONFIG-SYSTEM.
- tests/plugin-setup-error.test.ts /** * @story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md * @req REQ-ERROR-HANDLING - Gracefully handles plugin loading errors and missing dependencies */ - Mocks a rule module to throw on import, then requires ../src/index. - Expects console.error to log a clear rule load failure message. - Verifies a placeholder rule is created with meta.docs.description reflecting the failure. - Verifies placeholder rule.create() reports an ESLint error when traversing Program. → Directly validates REQ-ERROR-HANDLING at rule load time.
- tests/cli-error-handling.test.ts /** * @story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md * @req REQ-ERROR-HANDLING - Plugin CLI should exit with error on rule load failure */ - Spawns ESLint CLI with this plugin enabled via eslint.config.js. - Confirms non-zero exit code and appropriate error output when using traceability/require-story-annotation. → Validates CLI-level error handling and integration with ESLint CLI.
- tests/integration/cli-integration.test.ts /** * Tests for CLI integration functionality * @story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md * @req REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE - Validate plugin registers via CLI */ - Spawns ESLint v9 CLI with --no-config-lookup and --config eslint.config.js. - Runs multiple test cases over stdin code, using rules like traceability/require-story-annotation and traceability/require-req-annotation. - Asserts expected exit status (1 for missing annotations, 0 when annotations are correct, 1 for invalid story/req paths). → Demonstrates that the plugin loads and its rules are active via ESLint v9 flat config and CLI (REQ-ESLINT-COMPAT, REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE).

traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria and named requirements for story 001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP are implemented with concrete evidence: - The plugin is structured as a standard ESLint plugin module in TypeScript and compiled to lib/, with a dynamic rule registry and proper exports (rules, configs, maintenance), satisfying REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE, REQ-RULE-REGISTRY, REQ-TYPESCRIPT, and REQ-NPM-PACKAGE. - ESLint v9 flat config integration is in place via eslint.config.js, and CLI integration tests confirm that the plugin loads and its rules execute correctly under ESLint 9, addressing REQ-ESLINT-COMPAT and core functionality. - Error handling for rule load failures is explicitly implemented in src/index.ts and validated by unit tests and CLI error-handling tests, fulfilling REQ-ERROR-HANDLING and the story’s Error Handling acceptance criterion. - Test infrastructure is in place with Jest + ts-jest, a focused jest.config.js, and multiple tests that explicitly reference this story and its requirements (plugin-setup, plugin-setup-error, cli-error-handling, cli-integration), covering registration, load behavior, and CLI integration, meeting REQ-TEST-SETUP. - User-facing documentation (README, ESLint 9 setup guide) and internal development documentation (eslint-plugin-development-guide) clearly describe installation, configuration, flat-config usage, and plugin development, satisfying the Documentation and User Experience acceptance criteria. Given this evidence, the foundational ESLint plugin structure described in this story is present, tested, and documented; the story is considered fully implemented.
